Privacy Policy

Last updated: July 16, 2026

Turn Someday Into Day One ("the app") is a recovery companion. This page explains, in plain language, what information the app collects, where it lives, and who else ever sees it.

What we collect

When you create an account: your email address, a phone number if you choose to add one, and a password or PIN (stored as an irreversible hash — never in plain text, and never visible to us).

As you use the app: your recovery start date, journal entries, craving logs, mood check-ins, lesson progress, milestone history, and messages you send to Friendly (the AI companion). All of this exists so the app can function — to show your streak, resume your lessons, and let Friendly respond with real context.

Where it lives

This app is self-hosted: your data is stored in a local database on the server you (or whoever runs this instance) is running — not in a shared cloud service we control. If you're using an instance someone else operates, they are the ones storing your data, on their own server.

Who else sees it

Two outside services are used, and only for the specific job each does:

• Anthropic processes the messages you send to Friendly, in order to generate Friendly's replies. This only happens for the message itself — sent when you chat, nothing else is shared. Friendly is only available when the app operator has configured this connection.

• Stripe processes payment if you subscribe to a paid plan. Your card details go directly to Stripe — this app never sees or stores your full card number.

Your journal, craving logs, and personal notes are never sent to either of these services unless you paste them into a message to Friendly yourself.

We do not sell data. There is no advertising network or analytics tracker collecting your activity in this app.

Your controls

From Profile, at any time: Export my data downloads everything as a file. Delete my account permanently removes your account and all associated data from the server — this cannot be undone once confirmed.

Not a substitute for professional care

Friendly is a supportive tool, not a licensed therapist, doctor, or crisis service. In an emergency, or if you're in crisis, contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) or your local emergency number — not this app.

Who this app is for

This app discusses addiction, recovery, and related sensitive topics and is intended for adults. It is not directed at children under 18.

Changes

If this policy changes in a way that matters, we'll update the date above. Continuing to use the app after a change means you've seen and accepted the update.

Questions

Contact: turnsomedayintodayone@gmail.com

Terms of Service

Last updated: July 16, 2026

By creating an account and using Turn Someday Into Day One, you agree to the terms below.

What this app is

A recovery companion offering daily lessons, journaling, streak tracking, an AI chat companion (Friendly), and related tools. Free features remain free; some features require a paid Pro subscription.

Not medical or professional advice

Nothing in this app — including anything Friendly says — is medical, psychiatric, legal, or professional advice, and it does not create a therapist-patient or doctor-patient relationship. It is a self-help and support tool. If you are in crisis or danger, contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or emergency services immediately, not this app.

Your account

You're responsible for keeping your password or PIN confidential and for anything that happens under your account. You must be at least 18 years old to use this app.

Subscriptions & billing

Paid plans are billed through Stripe on a recurring basis until cancelled. You can manage or cancel your subscription from Profile.

Refunds

Monthly and yearly plans include 7 days free — you are not charged until the trial ends. Founding Lifetime is a one-time purchase with no trial. Either way, all sales are final and payments are non-refundable. Cancelling stops future billing and you keep Pro until the period you paid for ends.

Purchases made through Google Play or the App Store follow their refund policies, not this one.

Founding Lifetime is limited to 50 purchases. Once those are gone it is not offered again, at any price.

Every tool in this app is free to use without paying anything. Days 1–15 of every program, the SOS toolkit, the journal, the partner track and the meditation room cost nothing and never will.

Acceptable use

Don't use this app to harm others, attempt to break or abuse the service, or use Friendly's responses as a substitute for emergency care.

Your content

Your journal entries, messages, and other content you create belong to you. We don't claim ownership of it, and (per the Privacy Policy) don't sell it or use it to train anything beyond what's needed to run the app itself.

No guarantees

This app is provided "as is." Recovery outcomes are personal and cannot be guaranteed by any app. We aren't liable for decisions made based on the app's content, including Friendly's responses.

Ending your account

You may delete your account at any time from Profile. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms.

Changes

These terms may be updated; the date above reflects the latest revision. Continued use after a change means you accept the update.

Contact

Questions about these terms: turnsomedayintodayone@gmail.com

This is your private space — reflections you write here stay on this device (and sync to your account if you're signed in) but aren't shown to other users. Write with the same honesty you'd want to read from someone else.
Today's stories
A new set every day. These are written reflections — the things people in this room live through most often, put into words. They're not live posts, and the names aren't real people. (The live posts are up top.)

There's no commenting, replying or messaging anywhere in Rooms, and there won't be. That's deliberate. Recovery spaces online turn toxic fast — pile-ons, comparison, people preying on someone at their lowest. You can like a story to keep it. Nothing is sent to anyone, and nobody can reach you here.

For the one who loves you
Most people don't fail recovery because they're weak — they fail because they're unsupported. And most partners don't fail to support — they fail to understand, because nobody ever explained it to them. This page fixes that, for both of you.
Free — start here

A letter to the person who loves me

Written from your journey — send it and it opens their side too
5 things every partner should know
1. Addiction isn't about how much they love you — it stops feeling like a choice, and it's a pattern that formed long before you.
2. Shame is the fuel. Anger and silent disappointment feed it; understanding starves it.
3. Policing doesn't work. Safety to be honest does — "I'm struggling today" should never start a fight.
4. A slip is a lost battle, not a betrayal — and the days after a slip decide everything.
5. You matter too. Supporters need support — and sometimes their own quiet struggle deserves the same compassion.
Together — go deeper

Do this together

Welcome. You made a difficult decision — and it's the bravest one you've made in a long time.
You're on a path now — to better yourself, your life, and everything connected to it. Everyone who ever got free started exactly where you are: day one. If you slip, you keep going. Don't give up. It's in the dark where the work is done — and in the light where it's shown.
This is the 90-Day Bootcamp — an addiction program with continuous support: a counter that celebrates every milestone, lessons that meet you where you are, tools for the worst ten minutes, and real voices that read every lesson to you. You don't have to do this perfectly. You just have to do today.

Stress
You slipped. That's not the end of anything.
However this happened, it doesn't erase the days you already put in. What matters now is the next choice, not this one.
This is the moment that decides the next 24 hours — and you just chose to stay in the game. You don't have to be strong right now. You just have to not quit. Everyone who ever made it out has had this exact hour. What made them different was only what they did next.
A few honest next steps:
1. Get to a safe space, away from whatever's around you right now.
2. Reach out to one person you trust — even just to say what happened.
3. Reset your date when you're ready. No rush, no shame.

Panic Mode
You're safe right now, even if it doesn't feel like it. Let's slow this down together, one step at a time.
1. Put both feet flat on the floor. Feel the ground.
2. Splash cold water on your face or hold something cold.
3. Name out loud where you are right now.
4. Start box breathing below.

How this room works

Real people, one feed. Everyone here is working the same thing you are. You post, it stands. No replies, no DMs, no profiles — nobody can pile on and nobody can reach you.

Every post is checked first. A moderator reads every post before the room sees it. Honest struggle, anger, relapse — all welcome. Selling, cruelty, and graphic detail never make it in.

You're a first name and a day count. That's all the room knows about you.

Open 6am–10pm Central. Overnight the room sleeps — the SOS tools never do, and 988 is there any hour.

See something wrong? Tap Report. Two reports hide a post until a human looks.
